name: Hydroxyzine
summary: Hydroxyzine is a sedating first-generation antihistamine used in the United States for symptomatic relief of anxiety and tension, allergic pruritus, and peri-anesthetic sedation. This profile remains research-only while anxiety efficacy, QT/cardiac, sedation, interaction, duration-of-evidence, and regulatory evidence is assembled and reviewed.
description: Canonical hydroxyzine entity for evidence and safety integration. Publication remains held until indication-specific evidence, short- versus long-term anxiety boundaries, QT/Torsade risk, sedating interaction context, and regulatory provenance has passed the site’s review gates.
primary_effects_or_targets: histamine H1 receptor antagonism; sedating antihistamine effects
safety_notes: Current U.S. prescribing information contraindicates hydroxyzine in patients with a prolonged QT interval and warns about QT prolongation/Torsade de Pointes, drowsiness, and potentiation of central nervous system depressants. The label states that antianxiety effectiveness beyond four months has not been systematically assessed. This summary is not exhaustive; consult current product-specific prescribing information.
